title: Buddy Petit's later years
summary: Giles played a couple of jobs with Petit after he returned from across the lake; he praised Petit's triple-tonguing trumpet.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Did you ever play with Buddy Petit or did you hear him very much?
Well I played a job, a couple of jobs with Buddy Petit. At the last, after he had left and come back to New Orleans.

Where'd he been? I think Sammy Penn or someone told him, Sammy used to play for him. I think he said he went across the lake or act like he lived there with some relatives. Was it across the lake, Mandeville or anything? Do you know where it was?
That's right, that's right, Mandeville. He went over there. After he left-
He left the city then for a while. You could say he moved away like that. Yeah, he did. I wondered.

I think he went further than Mandeville, but I think he went around Bonk, Louisiana and all different parts. But at the last he stood over there until he come a while and played here until he got sick and he died. Yeah. You know, but he had stood away but he was one of the greatest trumpet players in the staff going, not above the staff but in the staff. He made such nice, triple-tongued stuff, you know, right in-
